proposals.before: He returned to the capital as a vice-director in the Ministry of the Treasury, received the honorary title Grand Master of Palace Leisure, held two vice-director posts in the war ministry's right and left secretariats in turn, and was then promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.
proposals.after: He returned to the capital as a vice-director in the Ministry of the Treasury, received the honorary title Grand Master of Palace Leisure, successively served as vice-director in the Right Office and in the Ministry of War, then as director in the Left Office and in the Ministry of War, and was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.
proposals.reason: Chinese 歷右司兵部二員外，左司兵部二郎中 means successive posts as vice-director of the Right Office and of the Ministry of War, then director of the Left Office and of the Ministry of War, not posts inside the war ministry's secretariats.

proposals.before: He entered the capital as vice-director in the Ministry of the Treasury, was given the honorary title Grand Master of Palace Leisure, served successively as two vice-director posts in the right and left secretariats of the Ministry of War, and was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.
proposals.after: He entered the capital as vice-director in the Ministry of the Treasury, was given the honorary title Grand Master of Palace Leisure, served successively as the two vice-director posts of the Right Office and the Ministry of War, then the two director posts of the Left Office and the Ministry of War, and was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.
proposals.reason: Same office-sequence error as the idiomatic line: 右司/左司 are the Left and Right Offices, distinct from the Ministry of War.

proposals.before: The emperor also recalled that Jiansu had long served in the Prince of Xiang's household and owed him an old debt of kindness, and approved the choice.
proposals.after: The emperor also recalled that Jiansu had long served in the Prince of Xiang's household and that there was an old favor between them, and approved the choice.
proposals.reason: 有舊恩 marks prior imperial favor toward Jiansu from his household service, not a debt Jiansu owed the emperor; the literal reverses the favor direction.

proposals.before: In the third month he was relieved of the left vice-directorship and of his duties in government, retiring with the title minister of justice.
proposals.after: In the third month he was appointed left vice-director, relieved of his duties in government, and retired with the title minister of justice.
proposals.reason: 除左僕射 in Tang bureaucratic narrative here means appointment to Left Pushe, not removal; he had been left chancellor (左相), not left pushe.

proposals.before: In the third month he was removed from the post of left vice-director, ceased serving in state affairs, and retired with the title Minister of Justice.
proposals.after: In the third month he was appointed to the post of left vice-director, ceased serving in state affairs, and retired with the title Minister of Justice.
proposals.reason: 除 normally means 'appoint to'; the concurrent 罷知政事 supplies the removal from real power.

proposals.before: For escorting the retired emperor to Shu, Jiansu was granted the title Pillar of State with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies and a fief of three hundred households.
proposals.after: For escorting the retired emperor to Shu, Jiansu was granted the title Equal in Ceremonial to the Three Excellencies (kaifu yitong sansi) and a fief of three hundred households.
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 is not 'Pillar of State' (柱國); it denotes the honor of establishing a staff with ceremonial parity to the Three Dukes.

proposals.before: For his merit in escorting the Retired Emperor on the tour to Shu, Jiansu was given the title Pillar of State with ceremonial honors equal to the Three Excellencies and an actual fief of three hundred households.
proposals.after: For his merit in escorting the Retired Emperor on the tour to Shu, Jiansu was given the title Equal in Ceremonial to the Three Excellencies and an actual fief of three hundred households.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 開府儀同三司 as Pillar of State.

proposals.before: Ti and E both reached the post of Attendant Gentleman; Yi ended as vice-director in the Ministry of Justice, and Guan as secretary in the Secretariat.
proposals.after: Ti and E both reached the post of Attendant Gentleman; Yi ended as vice-director in the Ministry of Justice, and Guan as secretary in the Palace Library.
proposals.reason: 秘書丞 belongs to the Palace Library (秘書省), not the Secretariat (中書).

proposals.before: As a youth he entered office by hereditary privilege as a palace guard attendant. After a favorable evaluation as magistrate of E County he was appointed magistrate of Wannian and rose through the posts of censor, remonstrance official, and secretariat director to Attendant Gentleman, left vice-director of the secretariat, vice-minister of revenue, censor-in-chief, and vice-minister of personnel.
proposals.after: As a youth he entered office by hereditary privilege as a palace guard attendant. After a favorable evaluation as magistrate of Hu County he was appointed magistrate of Wannian and rose through the posts of censor, remonstrance official, and gentleman of the Masters of Writing to Attendant Gentleman, left vice-director of the Department of State Affairs, vice-minister of revenue, censor-in-chief, and vice-minister of personnel.
proposals.reason: 鄠縣 is Hu County, not E; 尚書郎 is a Shangshu gentleman, and 尚書左丞 is left vice-director of the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat.

proposals.before: In youth he entered service by hereditary privilege as an armed attendant in the palace guard; from his evaluation as district magistrate of E he was graded for appointment and made magistrate of Wannian; he served successively as censor, remonstrance official, and secretariat director, and was promoted repeatedly to Attendant Gentleman, left vice-director of the Secretariat, vice-minister of revenue, censor-in-chief, and vice-minister of personnel.
proposals.after: In youth he entered service by hereditary privilege as an armed attendant in the palace guard; from his evaluation as district magistrate of Hu he was graded for appointment and made magistrate of Wannian; he served successively as censor, remonstrance official, and gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and was promoted repeatedly to Attendant Gentleman, left vice-director of the Department of State Affairs, vice-minister of revenue, censor-in-chief, and vice-minister of personnel.
proposals.reason: Same place and office mistranslations as in the idiomatic field.

proposals.before: When we set out from Mawei yesterday there were also arrangements made.
proposals.after: When we set out from Mawei the other day there were also arrangements made.
proposals.reason: 昨 here means “the other day / recently” in narrative, not necessarily the calendar day before.

proposals.before: Yuan abandoned the southern city and fled to Xiangyang, and an edict stripped him of his rank and fief.
proposals.after: Yuan abandoned the city and fled south to Xiangyang, and an edict stripped him of his rank and fief.
proposals.reason: 南奔 means fled southward, not abandoned the southern city; 棄城 and 南奔 are separate actions.

proposals.before: Yuan abandoned the southern city and fled to Xiangyang; an edict stripped him of his rank and fief.
proposals.after: Yuan abandoned the city and fled south to Xiangyang; an edict stripped him of his rank and fief.
proposals.reason: 南奔 is southward flight, not a southern city.

proposals.before: Cui Huan's grandfather Xuanwei had been ennobled as Duke of Boling for his service in the Shenlong coup.
proposals.after: Cui Huan's grandfather Xuanwei had been ennobled as Prince of Boling Commandery for his service in the Shenlong coup.
proposals.reason: 博陵郡王 is a commandery-prince (郡王), not a duke (公).

proposals.before: Cui Huan's grandfather Xuanwei was a meritorious servant of the Shenlong coup and was enfeoffed as Duke of Boling.
proposals.after: Cui Huan's grandfather Xuanwei was a meritorious servant of the Shenlong coup and was enfeoffed as Prince of Boling Commandery.
proposals.reason: 博陵郡王 must be Prince of Boling Commandery, not Duke of Boling.

proposals.before: His father Zhang was a noted scholar who rose to vice-minister of rites.
proposals.after: His father Qu was a noted scholar who rose to vice-minister of rites.
proposals.reason: 璩 is romanized Qu (Qú), not Zhang; the English personal name does not match the Chinese given name.

proposals.before: His father Zhang was renowned for literary learning and reached the post of vice-minister of rites.
proposals.after: His father Qu was renowned for literary learning and reached the post of vice-minister of rites.
proposals.reason: 璩 should be Qu, not Zhang.

proposals.before: In the first year of Zhenyuan (785) he personally performed the Southern Suburbs sacrifice and served as commissioner for the grand rites.
proposals.after: In the first year of Zhenyuan (785), when the emperor personally performed the Southern Suburbs sacrifice, Zong served as commissioner for the grand rites.
proposals.reason: 親祠南郊 is the sovereign's personal suburban sacrifice; 為大禮使 is Zong's office. The idiomatic English wrongly makes one subject do both.

proposals.before: In the first year of Zhenyuan, he personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburbs and served as commissioner for the grand rites.
proposals.after: In the first year of Zhenyuan, the emperor personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburbs; Zong served as commissioner for the grand rites.
proposals.reason: Same subject error as the idiomatic field: 親祠 belongs to the emperor; 為大禮使 belongs to Zong.

proposals.before: Du Hongjian was a clansman of the former chancellor Xian.
proposals.after: Du Hongjian was a clansman of the former chancellor Du Xian.
proposals.reason: Literal English drops the surname Du supplied by 杜鴻漸…故相暹 and by the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: More than a year later he was recalled as right vice-director of the secretariat, vice-minister of personnel, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and appointed commissioner of ritual.
proposals.after: More than a year later he was recalled as right vice-director of the Department of State Affairs, vice-minister of personnel, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and appointed commissioner of ritual.
proposals.reason: 尚書右丞 belongs to the Department of State Affairs (尚書省), not the Secretariat (中書省); the idiomatic English misidentifies the office.

proposals.before: After more than a year he was summoned and appointed right vice-director of the Secretariat, vice-minister of personnel, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and made commissioner of ritual.
proposals.after: After more than a year he was summoned and appointed right vice-director of the Department of State Affairs, vice-minister of personnel, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and made commissioner of ritual.
proposals.reason: 尚書右丞 is an office of the Shangshu sheng (Department of State Affairs), not of the Secretariat; the literal English mistranslates 尚書.

proposals.before: In the eighth month of the third year, Prince Jin of Dai became guardian of the eastern capital, deputy commander of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East, while retaining his grand councilorship.
proposals.after: In the eighth month of the third year, he replaced Wang Jin as guardian of the eastern capital, deputy commander of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East, while retaining his grand councilorship.
proposals.reason: 代王縉 means 'replaced Wang Jin', not 'Prince Jin of Dai'; the subject is Du Hongjian succeeding Wang Jin in these posts.

proposals.before: In the eighth month of the third year, Prince Jin of Dai became guardian of the eastern capital, served as deputy commander of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East circuits, and remained grand councilor as before.
proposals.after: In the eighth month of the third year, he replaced Wang Jin as guardian of the eastern capital, served as deputy commander of Henan, Huaixi, and Shannan East circuits, and remained grand councilor as before.
proposals.reason: 代王縉 is 'replaced Wang Jin' (代 + 王縉), not a princely title; English invents 'Prince Jin of Dai'.

decisions.after: He returned to the capital as a vice-director in the Ministry of the Treasury, received the honorary title Grand Master of Palace Leisure, successively served as vice-director of the Right Office and vice-director of the Ministry of War, then as director of the Left Office and director of the Ministry of War, and was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.
decisions.reason: The proposal correctly separates the Right and Left Offices from the Ministry of War, but the four successive posts should be stated individually so that each paired title cannot be mistaken for one combined office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 歷右司兵部二員外，左司兵部二郎中

decisions.after: He entered the capital as vice-director in the Ministry of the Treasury, was given the honorary title Grand Master of Palace Leisure, served successively as vice-director of the Right Office and vice-director of the Ministry of War, then as director of the Left Office and director of the Ministry of War, and was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.
decisions.reason: The proposed office parsing is correct, but naming each of the four posts separately is clearer and more literal than referring to two collective sets of posts.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 歷右司兵部二員外，左司兵部二郎中

decisions.after: The emperor also recalled that Jiansu had previously served in the household of the Prince of Xiang and had enjoyed his favor, and approved the choice.
decisions.reason: The repair correctly reverses the current mistranslation of 有舊恩. This wording makes clear that Jiansu had received the emperor's favor while serving his former princely household, rather than leaving the direction of the favor vague.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 上亦以經事相王府，有舊恩，可之

decisions.reason: 除左僕射 appoints Wei Jiansu as left vice-director; the distinct phrase 罷知政事 removes him from participation in government. The proposed sequence restores that contrast.
The literal field makes the same error by treating 除 as removal. The proposed wording correctly distinguishes appointment to 左僕射 from loss of governing authority.

decisions.after: For accompanying the retired emperor to Shu, Jiansu was granted the honor of opening an office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies and a fief of three hundred households.
decisions.reason: The proposal correctly removes the unrelated title 'Pillar of State,' but 開府 must not disappear from the replacement. The revised wording renders both the privilege of opening an office and its ceremonial parity, while 奉上皇幸蜀 is more naturally 'accompanying' the retired emperor to Shu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 見素以奉上皇幸蜀功，加開府儀同三司

decisions.after: For his merit in attending the Retired Emperor on his journey to Shu, Jiansu was granted the honor of opening an office with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies and an actual fief of three hundred households.
decisions.reason: The proposed correction removes 'Pillar of State' but omits the 開府 element of the honor. This version preserves that element and avoids implying that Jiansu conducted the imperial party as an escort.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 奉上皇幸蜀功，加開府儀同三司，食實封三百戶

decisions.after: Ti and E both reached the post of Attendant Gentleman; Yi ended as vice-director in the Ministry of Justice, and Guan as assistant director of the Palace Library.
decisions.reason: The proposal identifies the correct institution, but 丞 is the assistant-director post rather than a generic secretary. 秘書省 is the Palace Library, not the Secretariat.

decisions.after: As a youth he entered office by hereditary privilege as a palace guard attendant. After receiving a favorable evaluation as commandant of Hu County, he was appointed commandant of Wannian and rose through the posts of censor, remonstrance official, and gentleman of the Department of State Affairs to Attendant Gentleman, left vice-director of the Department of State Affairs, vice-minister of revenue, censor-in-chief, and vice-minister of personnel.
decisions.reason: The proposal fixes 鄠 and distinguishes 尚書省 from the Secretariat, but 縣尉 is a county commandant, not a magistrate. 'Gentleman of the Department of State Affairs' also identifies 尚書郎 more clearly than the proposed hybrid title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 自鄠縣尉判入等，授萬年尉，歷御史、補闕、尚書郎，累遷給事中、尚書左丞

decisions.after: In youth he entered service by hereditary privilege as an armed attendant in the palace guard; after his evaluation as commandant of Hu County qualified him for advancement, he was appointed commandant of Wannian; he served successively as censor, remonstrance official, and gentleman of the Department of State Affairs, and was promoted repeatedly to Attendant Gentleman, left vice-director of the Department of State Affairs, vice-minister of revenue, censor-in-chief, and vice-minister of personnel.
decisions.reason: The proposal correctly repairs the place name and State Affairs offices, but both occurrences of 尉 denote county commandants. The revision also makes 判入等 an evaluation qualifying him for advancement rather than an opaque grading formula.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 自鄠縣尉判入等，授萬年尉

decisions.after: Earlier, when we set out from Mawei, I also made arrangements.
decisions.reason: The proposal correctly recognizes that 昨 cannot mean the previous calendar day here: the court left Mawei before reaching Shu in the seventh month, whereas this speech follows the envoy's arrival in the eighth. 'Earlier' conveys the retrospective sense, and the first-person subject is supplied by the retired emperor's continuing speech.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 七月，至巴西郡……八月，肅宗使至……昨發馬嵬，亦有處分

decisions.reason: 棄城 and 南奔 are separate verb phrases: Cui Yuan abandoned the city and fled south. The current 'southern city' attaches 南 to the wrong phrase.
The literal field repeats the same attachment error. 南 modifies 奔, specifying southward flight to Xiangyang, rather than 城.
博陵郡王 is a commandery princely title, not a dukedom. The proposed title preserves the explicit 郡王 rank.
The literal field likewise mistranslates 郡王 as duke. 'Prince of Boling Commandery' restores the stated rank.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 崔渙，祖玄暐……封博陵郡王

decisions.reason: 璩 is Cui Huan's father's given name, Qu; 'Zhang' has no basis in the Chinese. The replacement agrees with the surname inherited from the surrounding Cui genealogy.
The literal field contains the same unsupported name. 璩 is read Qu and identifies Cui Huan's father.
The implicit subject of 親祠 is Emperor Dezong, while Cui Zong is the subject of 為大禮使. The proposal correctly separates the sovereign performing the sacrifice from the official administering its rites.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 貞元元年，親祠南郊，為大禮使

decisions.reason: The literal field wrongly assigns both actions to Cui Zong. In this regnal context the emperor personally performs the suburban sacrifice and Zong serves as grand-rites commissioner.
暹 refers to Du Xian, the former chancellor and senior clansman named by the shared surname 杜. Supplying the surname prevents an unnecessary ambiguity without changing the kinship claim.
尚書右丞 belongs to the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat. The proposed correction changes only the misidentified institution.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 徵拜尚書右丞、吏部侍郎、太常卿

decisions.reason: The literal field makes the same institutional error. 尚書省 is the Department of State Affairs; the neighboring reference to 二聖 in s0190 does not alter Du Hongjian's subject or office sequence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 尚書右丞……二聖晏駕，鴻漸監護儀制

decisions.reason: 代 is the verb 'replaced' and 王縉 is the official Wang Jin. The current reading invents a Prince Jin of Dai and wrongly makes him the sentence's subject instead of Du Hongjian.
The literal field repeats the segmentation error. Du Hongjian replaced Wang Jin as eastern-capital guardian and retained his own grand councilorship.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 三年八月，代王縉為東都留守

claimRetractions.reason: The accepted name repair establishes that 璩 is the given name Qu. The alternate-name claim 'Zhang' was created solely from the erroneous English and must not survive as an alias.
